chapter: Rabbit Foot show and show life
title: Playing breakers dances after the show
summary: Show bands played late dances after the last show but knew mostly show music, so audiences' requests were hard to meet.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: She was in her 30s and this was in her 20s. Did any of those minstrel bands ever play for any dances anyplace or anything else?
On the side or anything around?

Many nights after the last show we go play a dance. You would, really? Play what you call a breakers dance. Yeah, really. Yeah, well, we'll get together there and try to form something to play for the people you know, because you take a regular show band that is continuing to play shows and stay on the shows, while there's a lot of things happening out here in dance halls and auditors that passes over his head. Yeah. He doesn't know what's going on because he's constantly got his head in these books that the performers want him to play. You know what I mean? Well that's all he knew then, you see? Now when the season is closed, he get back out there with the musician that is in the field, there's a lot of songs he has to learn. Yeah, that's right. A lot of songs he should know, but he don't know them because he was participating in the show. So all he was playing was just show music. So he'd get out there, he'd learn those songs that he was doing. So we used to play these breakers dances and a lot of people come up and ask us to play certain songs, well we didn't know them, you know what I mean? We'd say, well we'll play what we know, well we'll play what we know and they'll satisfy them. We'll play plenty of breakers dances. And they'd pay extra money like that. Because a lot of people always was interested in hearing the show band. We hear the band play at the show last.
